newsitem.title: USA: Newborn baby found dead in gym bag in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Newborn baby found dead in gym bag in U.S.

text.p: Atlantic County authorities will await a full coroner's report before deciding whether to charge a Pennsylvania teenager in the death of a newborn baby found in a gym bag, a spokeswoman said Friday.
"We are waiting for a written report from the coroner and we can't do anything until we get it," said Janet Niedosik, a spokeswoman for the Atlantic County prosecutor's office.
Niedosik said a decision probably would not be made until next week. She declined to identify the mother, saying she was a juvenile.

A report in Friday's Philadelphia Inquirer said the coroner in Bucks County, Pennsylvania, where the baby was found dead in late May, has concluded that the baby girl was born alive but died afterward, most likely of suffocation.
Niedosik said the 17-year-old mother lives in Bucks County and was vacationing with her boyfriend's family at the Jersey shore, where she delivered the baby.
The article cited investigators as saying the mother cut the baby's umbilical cord after it was born in a bathtub, wrapped it in a towel and placed it in a gym bag.
She then allegedly put the gym bag in the trunk of her boyfriend's car for a two-hour drive, and hid the baby in the garage of her home, where police found the infant's body three days later.

The Inquirer cited coroner Thomas Rosko as saying the baby's death was caused by a combination of debris in her airway and improper positioning, which caused her neck to bend. He said the mother did not do "anything actively" to cause the death.
The mother also faces Pennsylvania charges of concealing a death.
